naslov: FMP stuns sluggish Crvena Zvezda to open ABA League season
tekst:
By Eurohoops Team/ info@eurohoops.net
FMP pulled off a major upset on Sunday. They stunned Crvena Zvezda Meridianbet 90–89 to open the 2026–27 AdmiralBet ABA League Regular Season, which started with Round 2 after previous postponements.
The visitors lacked defensive effort. FMP punished them for three quarters, reaching a double-digit lead, and held on down the stretch. Jamiya Neal poured in 27 points with five triples. Brandon Rush followed closely with 26 points. Down low, Nikola Gasic controlled the glass with a 13-point, 13-rebound double-double.
Zvezda’s head coach Ibon Navarro played without Andrej Bjelic, Ognjen Dobric, Johnathan Motley, Semi Ojeleye, and Nick Weiler-Babb at FMP Arena. On the bright side, Nikola Djurisic returned from injury for six points, and Patrick Baldwin Jr. made his brief debut. Chris Jones Jr. had a team-high 19 points, but it was not enough. The loss adds early pressure, following a 1–2 record in the EuroLeague.
Dubai cruises to easy victory in Slovenia
In later ABA action, Dubai dominated Perspektiva Ilirija 85–70 at Ljubljana’s Tivoli Hall.
Coach Xavi Pascual’s side led from start to finish, building a double-digit cushion in the first quarter despite sitting Awudu Abass, Justin Anderson, Davis Bertans, Mouhammadou Jaiteh, Mfiondu Kabengele, Dzanan Musa, and McKinley Wright IV.
Guard Davion Mintz delivered 20 points. This convincing regional victory adds to strong season momentum, alongside their current 2–1 record at the EuroLeague level.
Partizan beats Mega in ABA opener
After a 3–0 start in the EuroLeague, Partizan also opened its ABA League campaign with a win, defeating Mega 83–59 in both teams’ first regional game of the season. The game was played behind closed doors at Aleksandar Nikolic Hall due to a sanction imposed on Partizan last season.
Mega briefly led on several occasions in the first half, but Partizan took control with a 15–2 run in the second quarter and held a 42–33 halftime advantage. The hosts extended their lead after the break, entered the final quarter up 62–45, and maintained control until the final buzzer.
Ethan Thompson led Partizan with 21 points and seven rebounds. Nikola Tanaskovic added 14 points and six rebounds, while Joffrey Lauvergne contributed 10 points and five boards. Andrej Lucic scored 14 points for Mega, with Aleksandar Vojinovic adding 12 points and seven rebounds.
